rationale: Clinical delineation of Jaberi-Elahi syndrome (JABELS; OMIM #617988) across reported cohorts demonstrates that early-onset epilepsy and hyperkinetic movement disorders (including chorea, dystonia, and choreoathetosis) occur in a substantial proportion of affected individuals with biallelic GTPBP2 loss-of-function variants. These clinical features, alongside progressive microcephaly, neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA), and neuroectodermal/retinal involvement, reliably distinguish GTPBP2-related neurodevelopmental disorder from uncomplicated hereditary spastic paraplegias, which are characterized primarily by isolated lower extremity spasticity and weakness without early refractory seizures or prominent choreoathetosis.

evidence.text: Key clinical features in individuals with biallelic GTPBP2 nonsense variants include prenatal-onset microcephaly, tone abnormalities, movement disorders, epilepsy, dysmorphic features, retinal dysfunction, ectodermal dysplasia, and progressive brain iron accumulation.
